item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: TORONTO — The Ontario Superior Court of Justice has approved a $213.5 million class-action settlement against Sun Life. A news release from law firm Kim Spencer McPhee Barristers P.C. says the action began in 2010 regarding alleged improper administration of three universal life insurance policies, including Universal Plus, Flexiplus, and OptiMet. The policies were sold by Metropolitan Life Insurance Co. agents in Canada between 1987 and 1998. The release says Sunlife has denied any wrongdoing, and the company did not immediately respond to a request for comment after hours. The law firm says the settlement is the largest reported settlement in any life insurance policy dispute in Canadian history, concerning 70,000 eligible current and former Flexiplus and Universal Plus policyholders in Canada. Eldon Fehr, representative plaintiff, says the settlement will provide significant benefits to current and former Sun Life policyholders. This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 27, 2026 The Canadian Press

item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: OTTAWA — A Canadian official says there has been “limited progress” made in recent trade talks with the United States. Prime Minister Mark Carney on Tuesday acknowledged talks had intensified slightly in recent days and U.S. President Donald Trump and his officials have suggested a deal could be possible before next week midterm elections in the United States. But a Canadian government official with knowledge of the negotiations, who was not authorized to speak publicly about them, says today while discussions have continued, “there has been limited progress.” Diplomatic relations between Canada and the U.S. have been dicey since Carney’s government walked away from formal trade talks in August and the prime minister accused the Americans of making unreasonable last-minute demands. In response, Washington imposed tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian goods, and Ottawa followed up with retaliatory tariffs on American products. Trump announced Friday he will lift some of the 50 per cent tariffs on Canada at the end of the month, while adding tariffs to dozens of new products, including Canadian garbage and sewage. This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 27, 2026 With files from David Baxter in Ottawa and Aaron Sousa in Edmonton Catherine Morrison, The Canadian Press

item.title: Nova Scotia Power Announces Leadership Transition to new CEO
item.description: Nova Scotia Power today announced that Chris Smith has been named President and CEO of the utility, effective November 2, 2026. Currently Executive Vice President, Finance and Commercial, Chris joined ...
item.dc:creator: Business Wire
item.content:encoded: This press release is provided by Business Wire and is published as received. HALIFAX, Nova Scotia--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Nova Scotia Power today announced that Chris Smith has been named President and CEO of the utility, effective November 2, 2026. Currently Executive Vice President, Finance and Commercial, Chris joined Nova Scotia Power in 2017. Vivek Sood, who joined the company as CEO earlier this year, has announced his decision not to renew his contract. Over Vivek’s time as CEO, he provided steady leadership through a challenging period, helping to stabilize operations, rebuild trust and strengthen the focus on reliability, while moving important work like securitization forward. Vivek will work with Chris and the leadership team at Nova Scotia Power, ensuring these critical areas remain in focus through and after transition. Chris brings extensive utility experience and deep knowledge of the business to his new role. He has served in several senior executive roles throughout his time with Nova Scotia Power and was previously President of Heritage Gas (now Eastward Energy) before joining the company almost a decade ago. “On behalf of the Board, I’d like to thank Vivek for his leadership during a pivotal year for Nova Scotia Power, and to welcome Chris as CEO,” said Scott Balfour, Chair of the Nova Scotia Power Board of Directors. “Chris is a proven leader who deeply understands the business and the importance of maintaining focus on the priorities ahead. That includes supporting the new Nova Scotia Independent Energy System Operator through a complex transition in generation and system planning, while continuing Nova Scotia Power’s work to improve reliability and manage cost impacts for customers.” About Nova Scotia Power Nova Scotia Power has had a presence in communities across Nova Scotia for over a century. As the primary electricity provider in the province, the company is regulated by the Nova Scotia Energy Board and provides generation, transmission and distribution of electrical power to approximately 550,000 customers. This includes residential, commercial, and industrial customers across Nova Scotia. With 2,200 dedicated employees, the team at Nova Scotia Power works every day to provide safe, reliable service to customers in every corner of the province. Their focus is on engaging with communities about the important work being done to meet the evolving energy needs of Nova Scotians while supporting the exciting growth and development in the region. Nova Scotia Power Inc. is a wholly owned subsidiary of Emera Inc. (TSX/NYSE-EMA). Learn more at www.nspower.ca.
